questions.q: What is the capital of France?
questions.explanation: Paris has been the capital of France since the 10th century.

questions.q: Who was the first President of the United States?
questions.explanation: George Washington served as the first U.S. President from 1789 to 1797.

questions.q: Who wrote the 'Harry Potter' book series?
questions.explanation: J.K. Rowling wrote the Harry Potter series, published between 1997 and 2007.

questions.q: What planet is closest to the sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the closest planet to the sun.

questions.q: Which river is traditionally considered the longest in the world?
questions.explanation: The Nile, at about 6,650 km, is traditionally cited as the world's longest river.

questions.q: In which year did World War II end?
questions.explanation: World War II ended in 1945 with the surrender of Japan and Germany.

questions.q: What is the square root of 144?
questions.explanation: 12 x 12 = 144, so the square root of 144 is 12.

questions.q: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.explanation: Au comes from the Latin word for gold, 'aurum'.

questions.q: Which country has the most time zones (including overseas territories)?
questions.explanation: France spans 12 time zones due to its overseas territories, more than any other country.

questions.q: Who was the Byzantine Emperor during the fall of Constantinople in 1453?
questions.explanation: Constantine XI Palaiologos died defending Constantinople when it fell to the Ottomans in 1453.

questions.q: What is the value of pi rounded to 4 decimal places?
questions.explanation: Pi rounded to four decimal places is 3.1416.

questions.q: Who wrote 'One Hundred Years of Solitude'?
questions.explanation: Gabriel García Márquez published this landmark of magical realism in 1967.

questions.q: What is the atomic number of Uranium?
questions.explanation: Uranium has 92 protons, giving it atomic number 92.
